newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico livestock report, feeder export price - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico livestock report, feeder export price - USDA.

text.p: USDA reported Wednesday that around 5,600 head were exported into the United States at four crossing points Tuesday.
Through Santa Teresa, N.M., around 3,000 head of steer calves were sold firm to 1 cent/lb higher while yearlings sold steady.
"Trade active, demand good. Bulk of supply consisted of steers weighing 300-600 lbs, included in supply were 600 head of steers previously sold on video," USDA said.
Prices for 300-400 lb head were 86-96 cents/lb, although a few lots of 300 lb head at 97-99 cents/lb, 400-500 lb at 76-86 cents/lb and 500-600 lb at 74-76 cents/lb.

Through Nogales, Ariz., around 1,100 head were sold at steady prices for steer calves. Prices for 300-400 lb feeder steers were between 80-90 cents /lb and for 400-500 lb head they were between 75-80 cents/lb.

Through Laredo, Texas, around 800 head were sold at firm prices up to 2 cents/lb higher. Prices for 300-400 lb head were at 82-92 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb head at 72-82 cents/lb and for 500-600 lb head at 70-73 cents/lb.
Through Del Rio, Texas, around 400 head were sold, but not enough to form indicative prices. "Around 80 percent of cattle crossed consisted of corriente steers weighing 300-500 lbs," the USDA said.
